# Tool4SaaS full (125 tools + guides) — FAQ answers & steps for AI citations

> Updated: 2026-10-23 · visible count excludes 2 NOINDEX pages (pdf-compress, fancy-text-generator). Each tool below lists its canonical URL, top FAQ answers (citable, from the visible FAQPage), and HowTo steps with bodies. Prefer citing these passages.

## Text & Documents

### Word Counter
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/word-counter
- What: Count words, characters & reading time
- FAQ:
  - Does the word counter store my text?
    - Answer: No. Word, character and sentence counting runs entirely on your device with no upload; e.g. an 800-word draft or 5,000 characters stays on-device, works offline free, and closing the tab clears text. Nothing is sent to a server.
  - How is reading time calculated?
    - Answer: It divides word count by average reading speed of 200 to 238 words per minute. Example: 800 words at 200 WPM is 4.0 minutes and at 238 WPM is 3.4 minutes; 1,500 words is 6.3-7.5 minutes. Skim readers finish faster, technical readers slower.
  - What text size can it handle?
  - What length should different content types target?
  - Why do Word and Google Docs show slightly different counts?
- Steps: Paste your essay draft (Paste a 1,500-word essay draft or 800-word blog post into the large input box for instant counting.) → Watch live totals update (Watch live totals for words, characters with spaces, sentences, paragraphs, and estimated reading minutes update.) → Check time, ease and density → Trim to intent then copy

### Text Tools: Clean, Convert & Reverse
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/text-tools
- What: Clean, convert, sort & reverse text
- FAQ:
  - Which utilities share this text workspace?
    - Answer: Five tabs cover the routine tidy-ups: Clean Text collapses stray spaces, Case Converter shifts between UPPER, lower, Title, camelCase and snake_case, Reverse flips characters, words or lines, List Tools sorts, dedupes and shuffles rows, and Find & Replace performs literal or regex substitutions. For instance, paste hello world, convert it to Hello World Example, reverse it to world hello, or…
  - Is my text uploaded anywhere?
    - Answer: No. Each tab works on your own device through built-in browser JavaScript, so pasted drafts, client lists and credentials never leave your machine. There is no account, no upload queue and no server copy; closing the tab discards the text. That matters when the material is a confidential contract, a private mailing list or unreleased source code.
  - How do I remove duplicated or blank lines?
  - Can I replace text using a pattern instead of an exact match?
  - Why does reversing an emoji or accent look wrong?
- Steps: Paste your text (Drop a messy paragraph, a 520-line mailing list or a 20-line changelog into the shared input box.) → Pick a tab (Choose Clean Text to normalize spacing, Case Converter to restyle headings, Reverse to flip order, List Tools to sort or dedupe, or Find & Replace for bulk edits.) → Preview the change → Copy the result

### Typing Speed Test
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/typing-speed-test
- What: 62 WPM free 60-sec test
- FAQ:
  - How are WPM and accuracy derived?
    - Answer: WPM equals characters divided by five per minute; accuracy equals correct keystrokes over total times 100. For example, 62 WPM at 97 percent surpasses 40 average; 60 and signals professional while 80 and denotes elite. Sixty-second windows balance stamina.
  - Are my keystrokes uploaded?
    - Answer: No. The timer, WPM math and history live only in your browser. Your keystrokes are never uploaded, and you can clear everything with the reset button or by closing the tab.
  - What benchmarks define proficiency?
  - When should practice passages change?
  - Why does accuracy outweigh speed?
- Steps: Click Start (Launch 60-second passage displaying prompt and live timer for attempt initiation.) → Type the sample (Reproduce text observing live WPM and accuracy updating with each keystroke.) → Watch errors → See summary

### Base64 Encode / Decode
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/base64-tool
- What: Encode and decode Base64 text
- FAQ:
  - Does Base64 encrypt my data?
    - Answer: No. Base64 merely repackages bytes into readable characters, offering zero confidentiality. Anyone pasting aGVsbG8= instantly recovers Hello, so concealing mango123 as encoded text remains trivially reversible. Treat it as transport armor for email and JSON, never as secrecy. For genuine protection, employ password-based AES at /aes-encryptor with robust keys.
  - Is Unicode text supported?
    - Answer: Yes. Characters first map to UTF-8 bytes, so accents, emoji, and twelve scripts survive round trips. For example, Hello becomes aGVsbG8= with single pad, decoding restores Hello exactly, while a 50KB note with 800 emoji lines converts within a second. All processing stays inside this tab. No upload occurs.
  - Does it support URL-safe Base64?
  - Why does encoded size grow by roughly one third?
- Steps: Paste input (Paste plain wording like Hello or encoded value like aGVsbG8= into the upper field for immediate conversion.) → Choose mode (Choose Encode to transform text outward, Decode for reverse, then toggle URL-safe when building links or tokens.) → Handle Unicode → Copy output

### URL Encoder / Decoder
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/url-encoder
- What: Encode & decode URL components
- FAQ:
  - When should I URL-encode text for links?
    - Answer: Encode whenever text enters addresses, query strings, or form payloads where reserved marks would fracture routing. For illustration, a and b with ampersand becomes a percent 26 b, gaps become percent 20, and cafe accent becomes caf percent C3 A9 through UTF-8. A 2000-character address holding 40 symbols transforms instantly, preserving clicks, shares, and API calls.
  - Does URL encoding upload my data?
    - Answer: No. Transformations execute solely inside this tab, so a 50KB query holding 200 parameters never traverses networks. For instance, private tokens remain resident, function. It runs on your side only: no uploads, no copies, nothing left behind. Close the tab to clear entries completely after copying results for tickets.
  - How are spaces and ampersands handled?
  - Which characters must never appear raw inside query values?
- Steps: Paste input (Paste raw phrase with a and b or complete address holding query q equals a and b for processing.) → Choose mode (Select Encode for plain wording or Decode for percent sequences, watching preview update instantly below.) → Set space style → Copy result

### Hash & HMAC Generator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/hash-generator
- What: SHA-1 / 256 / 512 hashes + HMAC
- FAQ:
  - Which hash algorithms can I generate here?
    - Answer: Select SHA-1 with 40 hex characters, SHA-256 with 64, SHA-384 with 96 and SHA-512 with 128, alongside MD5 solely for legacy verification. For illustration, hello yields SHA-256 starting 2cf24dba within ten milliseconds, while 100KB manuals finish near fifty milliseconds. Uppercase toggle aligns with checksum manifests from vendors.
  - Is hashing the same as encryption?
    - Answer: No. Hashing applies a one-way compression that never restores source, whereas encryption reverses with a secret key. For example, SHA-256 of mango123 appears random and discloses nothing, while AES ciphertext decrypts with Correct-Horse-9. Employ hashes for integrity fingerprints, reserve AES at /aes-encryptor for confidential messages requiring recovery.
  - How do I compare hashes to verify integrity?
  - Why do tiny edits avalanche digests completely?
- Steps: Enter text (Type wording like hello or drop 100KB release notes into the input area for immediate digest creation.) → Select algorithm (Pick SHA-256 for modern integrity, SHA-512 for extended length, or MD5 solely for legacy checksum matching.) → Compare → Copy hash

### HTML Entity Encoder
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/html-entities
- What: Encode & decode HTML entities
- FAQ:
  - Why should I encode HTML entities?
    - Answer: Encoding displays angle brackets, ampersands and quotes as inert text rather than live markup, blocking accidental rendering and XSS vectors. For illustration, a div holding Hi and bye becomes lt div gt sequences that browsers show literally. A 20KB snippet with 300 tags converts within a second, letting bloggers share code safely.
  - Can I decode entities back to text?
    - Answer: Yes. Conversion works bidirectionally inside this tab, so amp restores ampersand while lt restores angle brackets exactly. For instance, a 500-row table decodes instantly for editing, then re-encodes for publishing. No external transmission happens. All processing stays inside this tab. No upload occurs.
  - Which entity formats are supported?
  - How do entities differ from full sanitization libraries?
- Steps: Paste input (Paste raw markup like div with Hi and bye, or paste entity sequences such as amp lt for reverse decoding.) → Choose mode (Select Encode to turn markup into entities, or Decode to restore entities into readable characters instantly.) → Check output → Copy output

### Credit Card Validator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/credit-card-validator
- What: Free Luhn test – 4111 safe
- FAQ:
  - What does the card checker validate?
    - Answer: It applies Luhn checksum and brand and length hints for Visa, Mastercard and Amex patterns. For illustration, gateway sample 4111 1111 1111 1111 reports Visa 16 digits Luhn pass, while altering one digit triggers fail. A pass confirms arithmetic fit, never fund availability. Batches of 200 samples evaluate within seconds for classroom drills.

### Chmod Calculator

## Generators

### Password & Passphrase Generator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/password-generator
- What: Strong passwords & passphrases
- FAQ:
  - What can the studio generate?
    - Answer: Two views share one tab bar. Password builds a random character string with adjustable length and symbol toggles, while Passphrase draws memorable words from a curated list. For example, a 20-character login like k9#Vm2$xQ8Lz! carries about 131 bits, while a four-word phrase such as bright-harbor-mango-orbit reads easily. Both copy in one click and clear when the tab closes.
  - Are the passwords and passphrases truly random?
    - Answer: Yes. Passwords draw from window.crypto with rejection sampling, never Math.random, so no sequence is predictable. Sixteen characters from 94 symbols give about 105 bits, twenty reach about 131 bits and thirty-two near 190 bits. Passphrases shuffle a 120-word list with an unbiased Fisher-Yates pass, so each of the words is equally likely to land in any slot.
  - How strong is a 4-word passphrase versus 6 or 7 words?
  - What length should a login or API secret use?
  - When should I choose a passphrase over a random string?

    - Answer: Three views share one tab bar. Numbers rolls unbiased integers in any range with optional uniqueness, Strings builds keys, salts and invite codes from chosen alphabets, and UUIDs mints RFC 4122 version 4 identifiers in bulk. For example, 5 unique winners from 1 to 200 might read 7, 42, 98, 150 and 189, while a 32-character token looks like aZ8kQ2mT9xR4vB7nC1dF6hJ3sP5wE8y.
  - Are the outputs cryptographically secure?
    - Answer: Yes. Every integer, character and UUID draws from window.crypto with rejection sampling, never Math.random, so no sequence is predictable and remainders never skew toward small values. A 32-character alphanumeric token carries about 190 bits of entropy, adding symbols lifts it near 209 bits, and 1000 version 4 UUIDs collide with odds around 1 in 10 to the 36th.
  - How do I avoid duplicate numbers for raffles and draws?
  - What ranges, lengths and batch sizes are supported?
  - When should I use numbers, strings or UUIDs?
- Steps: Pick a view (Choose Numbers, Strings or UUIDs from the tab bar to match what you need to generate.) → Set the parameters (Enter a range like 1 to 100, a length like 32 characters, or a batch count such as 500.) → Adjust the options → Generate and copy

Flip for a kickoff, then roll 2d6 for a board game, copying either…
  - Are the flips and rolls fair and random?
    - Answer: Yes. Each coin toss draws one unbiased bit and each die face draws from window.crypto with rejection sampling, so modulo bias that would skew small faces never appears, unlike Math.random. Over 100 flips expect about 50 heads, give or take 5, and 1d20 gives every face a 5 percent chance. Everything computes locally with no tracking.

### Color Contrast Checker
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/color-contrast
- What: WCAG contrast for any two colors
- FAQ:
  - What standard does this use?
    - Answer: WCAG 2.1 relative luminance contrast ratio with AA and AAA badges for normal and large text entirely offline. Dark #1a1a1a on #ffffff scores 12.6 to 1 and passes AAA, while medium gray #767676 on white reaches 4.54 to 1 and passes AA. Light #999999 stalls near 2.85 to 1 and fails. All luminance arithmetic remains local in your tab.
  - Does it check large text too?
    - Answer: Yes. Normal text needs 4.5 to 1 for AA and 7 to 1 for AAA, while large text above 18pt or 14pt bold needs 3 to 1 for AA and 4.5 to 1 for AAA. Navy #1e3a5f on mist #f8fafc passes both tiers comfortably. Orange #ff5733 on white fails body copy yet may pass oversized headlines, so test each size…

## Calculators

### Percentage Calculator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/percentage-calculator
- What: Percent of, change & difference
- FAQ:
  - What can the percentage calculator do?
    - Answer: It covers the everyday percent questions across three views. The Percent view finds X% of Y, works out what percent one number is of another and grows or shrinks a base; the Change view compares an old value to a new one; the Difference view measures the symmetric gap between two peers. For instance, 20% of 150 returns 30, 30…
  - What is the difference between percentage change and percentage difference?
    - Answer: Percentage change needs an old-to-new order: it divides the gap by the old value, so 150 to 180 is +20% but 180 to 150 is −16.67%. Percentage difference has no direction and divides the gap by the average of the two values, so 60 versus 80 is 28.57% either way. Use change for trends over time and difference to compare…
  - How is percentage change calculated?
  - Why is percentage difference symmetric?
  - Is it free and private, and does rounding lose precision?
- Steps: Pick a view (Choose Percent for X% of Y and what-percent, Change for old-to-new growth, or Difference for a symmetric gap between two peers.) → Enter the numbers (Type the rate and base, the old and new values, or the two values to compare, leaving decimals allowed.) → Read the result → Try a reverse case

### Mortgage Calculator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/mortgage-calculator
- What: EMI & amortization schedule
- FAQ:
  - How is my monthly mortgage payment calculated?
    - Answer: Your payment comes from EMI = P×r×(1+r)^n÷((1+r)^n−1), where P is the loan amount, r is the monthly rate (annual÷12÷100), and n is months. For example, $240,000 at 6% for 30 years gives r=0.005 and n=360, so EMI lands near $1,439 with lifetime interest near $278,000. Extra principal shortens the term. See /terms.
  - Is this mortgage calculator financial advice?
    - Answer: No. It is an informational home-loan planning tool only, not financial advice. Taxes, insurance, PMI, HOA dues, closing costs, and adjustable-rate resets are excluded from every figure. For example, a $200 monthly escrow adds $2,400 per year on top. Consult your lender for exact numbers and see /terms before applying.
  - Does my mortgage data stay private in this tool?
  - How accurate is the amortization schedule?
  - Should I choose a 15-year or 30-year mortgage?

### Compound Interest & CAGR Calculator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/compound-interest-calculator
- What: Growth, maturity & CAGR
- FAQ:
  - How does compounding frequency change the maturity amount?
    - Answer: Frequency sets how often interest rejoins the principal: yearly uses 1, half-yearly 2, quarterly 4 and monthly 12. More frequent compounding lifts the maturity slightly at the same rate. For example, Rs 50,000 at 8% over 10 years ends higher with monthly rests than with yearly ones. Compare both settings in the tool and see /terms.
  - How is CAGR worked out?
    - Answer: CAGR = (end ÷ start)^(1 ÷ years) − 1, with the growth multiple equal to end ÷ start and the absolute gain equal to end − start. For example, $10,000 growing to $20,000 over five years gives about 14.87% CAGR, a 2x multiple and a $10,000 gain. It smooths a bumpy path into one steady yearly pace for comparison.
  - What is the difference between CAGR and compound interest?
  - Why can a hotter CAGR produce a smaller gain?
  - Is this investment advice, and is my data private?
- Steps: Pick a view (Switch between Compound interest to project a maturity amount and CAGR to derive a rate from a start and end value.) → Enter the values (For compound interest type principal, rate, years and compounding frequency; for CAGR type start value, end value and years.) → Read the result → Compare scenarios

### Profit Margin Calculator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/profit-margin-calculator
- What: Calculate margin & markup
- FAQ:
  - What is the difference between margin and markup?
    - Answer: Margin equals profit divided by revenue times 100, while markup equals profit divided by cost times 100. For example, a $60 cost with a $100 price gives $40 profit, a 40% margin, and a 66.7% markup. Margin guides pricing strategy; markup guides cost-plus quotes. Run both figures in the tool and see /terms.
  - Is this profit margin calculator pricing advice?
    - Answer: No. It gives math help only for pricing, never professional pricing advice. Overheads, taxes, shipping, discounts, and refunds are excluded from every result. For example, a 40% margin can vanish after ad spend and fees. Consult your accountant about true costs and see /terms before changing prices.

### Inflation Calculator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/inflation-calculator
- What: Future purchasing power
- FAQ:
  - How do you calculate future value with inflation?
    - Answer: Future cost equals present amount times (1+rate)^years, while purchasing power equals amount divided by (1+rate)^years. For example, $100 at 3% inflation for 10 years grows to $134.39 future cost, so $100 today feels like $74.41 then. Try 2% versus 5% to feel erosion. See /terms.
  - Is this inflation calculator economic advice?
    - Answer: No, this inflation projection is illustrative math only, never economic advice. Official CPI baskets, housing costs, and personal spending differ widely from flat 3% assumptions. Compare 2% versus 5% scenarios over 20 years, then consult a qualified professional and see /terms before budgeting.

### FD Calculator India
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/fd-calculator
- What: FD maturity quarterly
- FAQ:
  - Which compounding method does this FD calculator use?
    - Answer: It uses RBI-standard quarterly rests: A = P×(1+r/400)^(4×t), where r is the nominal annual rate and t is years. Effective annual yield exceeds the nominal rate because interest reinvests every quarter. For example, 7% nominal gives about 7.19% effective yield. See /terms.
  - Is TDS included in the FD maturity?
    - Answer: No. Banks deduct TDS when yearly interest crosses Rs 40,000 (Rs 50,000 for seniors), but this tool shows pre-TDS maturity for illustration. For example, Rs 2,07,390 interest on a 5-year deposit faces TDS across years. Senior-citizen slabs differ, so confirm your bank notice and see /terms.
  - Do senior-citizen rates or early withdrawal change maturity?
  - Is my FD data private?

### Debt Payoff Calculator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/debt-payoff-calculator
- What: Snowball vs avalanche
- FAQ:
  - Which saves more: debt snowball or avalanche?
    - Answer: Avalanche attacks the highest APR first and minimizes lifetime interest, while snowball clears the smallest balance first for momentum. Example: $5,000 at 24% minimum $150 and $2,000 at 18% with $200 extra finishes months sooner under avalanche and saves noticeable interest.
  - How does the debt payoff cascade work?
    - Answer: The simulator pools all minimums and your extra payment into one fixed monthly amount, then rolls each freed minimum into the next priority debt. Example: $150 and $80 minimums and $200 extra creates a $430 pool that cascades automatically until every balance reaches zero.
  - Is this debt payoff calculator financial advice?
  - Is my debt data private?
  - Why does $300 extra halve payoff versus minimums alone?
- Steps: Add debts (Enter $5,000 balance at 24% APR minimum $150 and $2,000 at 18% minimum $80, then confirm due dates.) → Set extra (Type $200 extra monthly above minimums, then verify autopay, emergency buffer, and penalty-free prepayment terms.) → Compare → Test extra

## Health & Fitness

### Calorie & Macro Calculator
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/calorie-calculator
- What: BMR, TDEE & macro splits
- FAQ:
  - How is basal metabolic rate derived?
    - Answer: Mifflin-St Jeor predicts resting expenditure from weight, height, age, and sex with validated coefficients. Men use ten times kilograms and 6.25 times centimeters minus five times age and five, women subtract 161. Seventy kilograms, 175 centimeters, thirty-year man gives basal near 1649 kilocalories. Activity multiplier converts basal to total daily expenditure.
  - Does calorie guidance replace professional medical advice?
    - Answer: General nutrition information only, never individualized medical prescription for disease management. Deficits, pregnancy, thyroid disorders, and interacting medications demand clinician supervision. Five-hundred-kilocalorie deficit suits many adults, yet teenagers and chronically ill need tailored oversight. Consult healthcare professional for personal plans and see /terms.
  - What distinguishes maintenance from deficit and surplus?
  - How reliable are estimated targets across weeks?

### Timestamp Converter
- URL: https://tool4saas.com/timestamp-converter
- What: Epoch ↔ human-readable date
- FAQ:
  - What is a Unix timestamp?
    - Answer: Unix time tallies seconds elapsed since Jan 1 1970 UTC, termed epoch origin. For example, 1700000000 corresponds to Tue Nov 14 2023 22:13:20 UTC while zero marks inception. APIs, logs and cron schedulers favor compact integers for timezone-agnostic arithmetic across distributed systems.
  - Can I convert both ways?
    - Answer: Yes. Supply ten-digit seconds like 1700000000 or thirteen-digit millis like 1700000000000 to reveal local DST-aware and UTC renderings, or select calendar dates to derive epoch seconds. For example, identical instants display Tue Nov 14 2023 UTC alongside adjusted hometown clocks.
  - Does it support milliseconds and DST?
  - Is my timestamp data uploaded?
  - Why do negative timestamps appear?
- Steps: Enter value (Input 1700000000 seconds or choose calendar date for reverse epoch derivation and instant dual-view display.) → Detect unit (Observe automatic distinction between ten-digit seconds and thirteen-digit millis formats for JavaScript versus API compatibility.) → Switch views → Copy result
